statement: The first line holds n; the second holds n deadlines (day numbers from 1); the third holds n profits. Each job takes one day, pays its profit only if finished by its deadline, and only one job runs per day. Print two numbers: the maximum count of jobs done and the maximum total profit, separated by a space. Sort by profit descending and drop each job into the latest free day at or before its deadline; skip it when no such day remains. Late placement keeps early days open for tight deadlines.

example.why: The 40-profit job takes day 1; the 20-profit job, deadline 4, takes day 4; the rest find day 1 occupied.

hint: For each job scan days deadline, deadline-1, down to 1 and grab the first free one.
mistake: Placing rich jobs on the earliest free day - that squanders exactly the days tight-deadline jobs need.
